meta.title: Strategic chokepoints
meta.source: U.S. EIA World Oil Transit Chokepoints (list of named straits/canals); coordinates from Wikidata (CC0)
meta.license: EIA information is U.S. government work (public domain). Wikidata coordinates: CC0.
meta.note: Eight entries follow the EIA oil-transit chokepoint list. Four extra maritime chokepoints are labelled as such. Locations are the Wikidata coordinate of the named feature, not a shipping-lane centerline.
meta.attribution: U.S. Energy Information Administration, World Oil Transit Chokepoints; Wikidata contributors (CC0)

items.note: Busiest oil chokepoint, between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.
Main shipping lane between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea.
Links the Red Sea and the Mediterranean. EIA groups this with the SUMED pipeline.
Links the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden / Arabian Sea.
The Danish straits (including the Great Belt and Øresund) connecting the Baltic Sea to the North Sea.
Bosporus and Dardanelles, linking the Black Sea to the Mediterranean.
Links the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans across the Isthmus of Panama.
Listed by EIA as an alternative route around southern Africa when other chokepoints are disrupted.
Entrance to the Mediterranean Sea; widely cited strategic maritime chokepoint (not on EIA's oil-transit list).
